text:
maria: Heads-up: onboarding lavender9b (int4) today. initial canary shows intermittent OOMs at ~max_new_tokens=1024 with batch_size=4. memory pattern looks like fragmentation rather than steady leak. sharing logs shortly

sam: thx. can you paste heap snapshot / node logs? is this on the dedicated canary pool or hosted lane?

maria: hosted canary. attaching snippet from runtime: 
```
E | gpu0 | alloc failed after 12.3s | attempted=1.9G used=1.72G free_holes=3 largest_hole=128M
W | kv_cache | evict triggered: dropped 3 entries
I | batch | processed 3 requests, 1 waiting
```

kevin: looks like allocator fragmentation + big prefix KV glue. lavender's tokenizer tends to produce long prefixes for our evals. are we using prefix caching?

maria: yes, prefix cache on. we enabled prefetch=on during quantized run to mitigate coldstart. turning it off for a smoke now.

ava: hypothesis: int4 kernel switch for attention creates transient large temporary buffers during rotary / softmax path. combined with prefetch+batching => temporary high watermark. try microbatching (batch_size=2) and reduce prefetch concurrency to 1.

sam: also try lowering default max_new_tokens to 512 for hosted canaries — many workloads only need summary lengths. that reduces peak.

maria: ran microbatch w/ prefetch=1 and batch_size=2. no OOM for ~50 requests, latency bumped +12ms p50. logs: 
```
I | gpu0 | alloc success | used=1.35G free_holes=6 largest_hole=240M
I | batch | processed 2 requests, 0 waiting
```

kevin: good sign. next: test with simulated long-conversation prompts to stress KV. add kv_trim_threshold=0.6 (trim older prefixes earlier) and enable incremental compaction.

maria: applied kv_trim_threshold=0.6 on canary. observed slight quality blip on long-chat evals (regression ~1.8% rouge).

ava: expected tradeoff. Can we do adaptive trim: only trim when free_holes < X or before batch spike? That keeps quality for steady flows and frees memory under pressure.

sam: runtime can add heuristic: if free_holes < 200MB then trigger aggressive trim for next 2s. we can ship as config flag `adaptive_kv_trim=true` to hosted canary.

maria: toggled adaptive_kv_trim=true and kept max_new_tokens=512, batch_size=2, prefetch=1. ran 1k requests through canary set. OOMs = 0. latency +8ms overall, rouge regression -> 0.5% (within eval tolerance).

kevin: nice. two prod recommendations: 1) set hosted default for lavender9b to max_new_tokens=512, 2) enable adaptive_kv_trim with kv_trim_threshold=0.6 and prefetch_concurrency=1. keep batch default at 2 but allow customers to opt-in back to 4 if they accept risk.

ava: also add monitoring alert: if successful_evictions/sec > 5 and free_holes < 256MB for >30s, create auto rollback to fallback model variant (lavender9b-onnx32) to avoid customer-visible OOMs.

infra-bot: deploy plan created: canary -> 5% hosts -> 20% hosts -> full. feature flags: lavender9b.defaults.max_new_tokens=512, lavender9b.runtime.adaptive_kv_trim=true, lavender9b.runtime.prefetch_concurrency=1.

maria: i'll write the runbook steps and a short notes doc for support (including commands to force kv_compact and rollback variant). thanks all. :thumbsup:

kevin: one follow-up: add an eval job that runs a mixture of long-chat and summarization prompts nightly to detect quality drift from trims/quantization. small regression quickly flags.

maria: on it — i'll add the eval into nightly-suite and link PR when ready.

ava: great teamwork. :rocket:
